Tagging pipeline resilience design is excellent: per-phase timeout budgets with explicit floor semantics (lookup floor, Phase-1 floor, Phase-5-from-Phase-1 fallback), tested via an injectable phase-callables seam with fakeAsync hang simulation — degradation is graceful and pinned, never silent corruption.

The parsing-ml subsystem has real golden-dataset regression coverage (test/golden/parsing_golden_dataset.json, crf_ingredients.json, tagging_golden_test) plus a Viterbi calibration baseline — intent-level correctness is tracked, not just green status.
Fail-closed integrity on remote ML artifacts: SHA-256 hash registry for ONNX/CRF downloads refuses unverifiable models rather than silently accepting them.

ParseEventLogger closes a genuine feedback loop: per-attempt tier/domain/cost telemetry feeds site_configs success counters and even self-reports its own logging failures (parseEventLogFailed) — the strongest observability pattern in the chain, worth replicating on the correction-upload and share-sheet paths.

Cost discipline is real and layered: deterministic parsers first, selective ingredient-only LLM enhancement (~500 vs ~3000 tokens) before full LlmTier, client+server rate limiting with cost ceilings, and a documented single-retry-owner policy (ADR-001) — the double-LLM finding is a wiring gap between two good systems, not an absent philosophy.
PII defense-in-depth on the LLM boundary: mirrored Dart/TS scrubbers synced via a shared fixture vector file, server-side re-scrub, and heavy-redaction drop on corrections.

CRF ingredient-parser accuracy is genuinely CI-gated: the test/evaluation suite enforces an all-fields-exact >=85% floor against a 433-entry golden set on every PR (test.yml, BUT-1443) — a real accuracy regression gate, not just green-status.

tagging_pipeline_runner_test.dart demonstrates the correct mocking boundary: phase callables are injected while TagGenerator.assembleResult stays real, and per-phase timeout budgets (5s/10s/8s) plus partial-assembly behavior are pinned with fakeAsync — exemplary 'mock dependencies, not the subject'.

menu_personalization_test.dart includes a statistical behavioral test (20 simulated weeks x 3 fixed seeds, 60% max-share diversity floor) running the REAL MenuService generation path, plus an explicit cross-cutting invariant test that every personalization ceiling stays below the rating ceiling.

recipe_parser_service_test.dart pins the tier short-circuit threshold on both sides of the 0.65 boundary (0.65 stops, 0.649 continues), the security gate, LLM cost gating, and the cache circuit breaker — contract-level tests that would fail under real bugs.

Cloud Functions CI runner (functions/scripts/run-ci-unit-tests.js) auto-discovers all test:* scripts, refuses to pass vacuously on zero suites, and currently has an empty exclusion set; verified all 90 __tests__/*.test.ts files are wired to a script — no orphaned CF tests.

PII-scrubber Dart/TS parity is enforced via a shared fixture (pii-heuristic-vectors.json) tested on both sides, and prompt-changelog-guard.test.ts structurally forces a changelog entry per PROMPT_VERSION bump.
Phase-1 allergen tests pin the tri-state safety contract including the coverage<1.0 → UNKNOWN safety floor, kept in a dedicated file separate from generic tagging tests.

The site-config loop is a genuinely closed, automatic flywheel: logParseEvent increments per-domain success/failure counters (functions/src/events/log-parse-event.ts:234-249), SiteConfig.computedQualityScore switches from manual estimate to live success rate once >=5 samples exist (lib/models/parsing/site_config.dart:93-101), and isReliable feeds back into RecipeParserService's LLM-avoidance threshold (recipe_parser_service.dart:312-317). Capture -> measure -> behavior change, no human in the loop.

Alias learning (analyze-corrections.ts) is a real automatic model-data update with sensible anti-poisoning: corrections only become live ingredient aliases after 3 distinct users agree AND the target resolves to a known ingredient, applied transactionally.

Parse quality is measurable in production today: parse_events + daily-snapshots.ts (analytics/parsing_corrections/daily), detect-anomalies.ts (parsing_corrections_total), and the live admin dashboard's Parsing-detaljer tab give the founder a working measurement surface — the gaps are in coverage (URL-only), not in the plumbing.

LLM-side observability discipline is strong: every Gemini call logs structured completion events with promptVersion/experimentBucket/token counts, prompt edits are gated by a changelog test (prompt-changelog-guard.test.ts), and out-of-enum drift triggers explicit warnings — the prompt half of the loop is measure-ready even though A/B experiments aren't yet running.

The retrain half exists at all: a working corrections->CoNLL->CRF pipeline (scripts/crf/) plus golden-dataset regression tests and a hash-gated remote weight loader is far more flywheel infrastructure than most pre-launch solo projects have; the findings above are mostly about connecting built pieces, not building new ones.

Correction capture is privacy-hardened end-to-end (client scrub, server re-scrub, heavy-redaction drop, hashed IDs, deny-all rules with tests) — the flywheel won't become a GDPR liability as it scales.

The escalation ladder genuinely honors 'deterministic before LLM': 7-tier URL waterfall puts Gemini at tier 6, and RecipeParserService's selective ingredient enhancement patches only uncertain lines (~500 vs ~3000 tokens) before falling back to a full LLM extraction — verified in recipe_parser_service.dart and llm_tier.dart.

The cross-user GlobalRecipeCache with per-source TTLs (90-180 days) means each popular URL is scraped/LLM-parsed roughly once for the whole user base — the single biggest structural cost saver in the pipeline (modulo the retag write-back gap filed above).

Tagging is 100% deterministic (rule engine over an in-memory ingredient index, zero LLM), with per-phase timeout budgets and graceful degradation — the highest-volume operation in the app costs no marginal cloud money beyond the ingredient-cache load.

Defense-in-depth spend controls exist at four layers: client rate limiter with cost ceilings, server per-minute token buckets, dual Firestore kill switches (aiEnabled/llmParserEnabled), and ADR-001's 'server never retries Gemini' rule with the one OCR retry explicitly budget-gated at 65s remaining.

Cost observability was designed in, not bolted on: every Gemini exit path logs duration/tokens/promptVersion/bucket via structured Cloud Logging events, and llm_response_samples carries a GDPR-documented TTL — the plumbing for cost/quality dashboards is real even where consumers lag.
gemini-2.5-flash-lite as the model choice keeps worst-case per-call cost in tenths of a cent, so even the rate-limit gaps flagged above are bounded in absolute terms.
